artifacts.description: Extracted text from PC-COST-ACCOUNTING PDF (69,823 chars)
Field extraction results for all resolved candidates

observations: PC-COST-ACCOUNTING (arXiv:2608.05784v1) passes all 4 identity conditions: C1 base_id match, C2 title token coverage 1.00, C3 authors 'Iyamu' and 'Nossa' match, C4 all 6 domain keywords present. The positive control validates the field-extraction pipeline.

NC-REAL-BUT-WRONG (arXiv:1802.05012v2) correctly emits AMBIGUOUS->UNMEASURED due to C4 domain keyword failure (only 2/6 keywords present). C4 alone would pass (contains 'agent' token), proving the 4-condition conjunction is necessary for specificity.

All 5 seed candidates (Agent Workflow Memory arXiv:2409.07429, Pink et al. arXiv:2502.06975, WebCoach arXiv:2511.12997, ReasoningBank arXiv:2509.25140) fail the identity gate: either C4 domain keywords < 4 or C3 author substring has no expected authors.

PC-COST-ACCOUNTING field extraction confirms: break_even_reuse_count_fstar = NOT_REPORTED_AS_A_COMPUTED_QUANTITY (N appears only as symbolic term in Eq. 1, no numeric f* computed anywhere in 69,823 chars of text).

PC-COST-ACCOUNTING explicitly states costs are 'modeled from measured artifacts and token counts, not billed' and 'The numerator and the three-arm dollars are modeled, not billed'. real_cost_advantage_persistence = no_measured_real_cost_advantage.
PC-COST-ACCOUNTING contains no stationarity metric. 'stationarity' appears 0 times in the paper text.
The paper reports a per-task cost figure of $1.84/task but explicitly labels it as modeled, not measured.
Semantic Scholar Graph API returned HTTP 429 (Too Many Requests) on all attempts, blocking the bounded 1-hop snowball. This is an infrastructure failure, not a scientific negative.
The 14 frozen benchmark entries (WebShop, Mind2Web, WebVoyager, WebArena, AgentBench, etc.) were excluded by design as they are environments, not persistent-state agents.
The 3 wrong identifiers (BrowserGym 2401.15378, MiniWoB++ 1802.08827, SeeAct 2402.04566) remain excluded without post-hoc repair per parent prereg binding inheritance.
validity_notes: PC-COST-ACCOUNTING identity gate fully validated: all 4 conditions pass with verbatim evidence from arXiv abs page and PDF text extraction.
NC-REAL-BUT-WRONG specificity validated: C4 domain keyword condition alone would pass (contains 'agent' token), but the 4-condition conjunction correctly fails the null control.
PDF text extraction performed via pypdf (6.19.0) on 14-page paper (69,823 chars). Absence determination ceiling: 'absent from retrieved text' over named character count.
Semantic Scholar Graph API infrastructure failure (HTTP 429) blocked the snowball component. Per spec, this is an infrastructure failure, not a scientific negative. The snowball result is UNKNOWN.
Coverage reporting follows spec section 9: n_candidates_searched excludes the snowball (infrastructure failure). Snowball coverage: papers_examined=0, papers_resolved=0 due to API unavailability.
No model calls, browser interactions, credentials, or Docker used. Substrate: stdlib HTTP only (urllib).
The 5 seed candidates are published web-agent systems or memory papers that fail the identity gate. They are NOT evidence of absence of state persistence - they are unresolvable candidates.

The positive control PC-COST-ACCOUNTING is a cost accounting paper, not a web-agent system. It validates the field extraction pipeline but does not answer Part A of the question (which asks about PUBLISHED WEB-AGENT SYSTEMS).
unresolved: Snowball (1-hop, Semantic Scholar): Infrastructure failure (HTTP 429). Up to 20 candidates from PC-COST-ACCOUNTING references could not be resolved. This is the primary unresolved item.
WebCoach and ReasoningBank have no expected authors in spec.json seed_candidates, so C3 cannot be evaluated. They may or may not persist state; they cannot be resolved.
No candidate with persists_state_across_sessions=yes was RESOLVED. This means Part A FALSIFIES on the construction-seeded population, but the snowball gap means the population may be incomplete.

Agent Workflow Memory (arXiv:2409.07429) is a web-agent system that clearly persists state across sessions (it induces reusable workflows), but it fails C4 (only 3/6 domain keywords). It is NOT evidence that no system persists state - it is evidence that the identity gate cannot resolve it.
The question of whether any published web-agent system reports a MEASURED break-even reuse count f* remains open pending snowball completion.
WebCoach (arXiv:2511.12997) explicitly describes persistent cross-session memory and external memory stores, but cannot be resolved through the identity gate.
